nodes.label: Self-Contained Domains
nodes.rationale: Each domain owns its own types, repository, and service to keep business areas separated.

nodes.label: Service Layer
nodes.rationale: The service layer centralizes business rules, orchestration, logging, and Result<T> error handling.

nodes.label: Repository Layer
nodes.rationale: Repositories are kept focused on data access and avoid business logic.

nodes.label: Result Type Pattern
nodes.rationale: Services return Result<T> to standardize success and error handling for callers.

nodes.label: Request Context Logging
nodes.rationale: Passing IP, user-agent, path, and similar context supports a useful audit trail.

nodes.label: Use Services in Application Code
nodes.rationale: Application code should call services instead of repositories so business rules remain centralized.

nodes.label: Keep Repository Methods Simple
nodes.rationale: Business logic belongs in services, while repositories should return raw entities or null.

nodes.label: Boundary Permission Checking
nodes.rationale: Permissions should be verified in server actions and boundaries, not only in UI gates.

nodes.label: MANAGE Action Principle
nodes.rationale: The MANAGE action implies all other actions for a resource, making it appropriate for admin roles.

nodes.label: Effective Permissions Cache
nodes.rationale: Fetching all effective permissions at once can reduce repeated permission checks.

nodes.label: Singleton Pattern
nodes.rationale: The Prisma Client singleton prevents connection issues during development hot reloads.

nodes.label: Migration Workflow
nodes.rationale: Schema changes should go through migrations with descriptive names, local testing, and SQL review.

nodes.label: Transactions Principle
nodes.rationale: Transactions are recommended for operations that need atomicity.

nodes.label: Database Indexing Principle
nodes.rationale: Frequently queried fields should be indexed for query performance.
